# Compact ingestion trial failed the full-process throughput gate

The trial did not establish a 9× improvement. **0 origins completed the required analysis → independent review → local and standalone retrieval → shared publication sequence inside the trial.**

| Measure | Result |
|---|---:|
| Fresh selected origins | 132 |
| Producer records submitted | 20 |
| Independently accepted records | 19 |
| Accepted record with a known omitted-test correction | 1 |
| Accepted without that known exception | 18 |
| Partial record awaiting review | 1 |
| No producer record | 112 |
| Reviewed structural units | 22 |
| Reviewed target bytes | 16,935 |
| Published inside the trial | **0** |
| Full-process rate | **0 origins/hour** |
| Review-stage rate excluding the known exception | 72 origins/hour |
| Required full-process rate | 524.471 origins/hour |

The 72/hour figure uses the full 15-minute window and excludes publication. It is **not** an estimate for the two full repositories. Completion favored small files; the large files remained unfinished. Even this incomplete measure did not reach the target.

## Clock and scope

Setup began at 22:32:50 UTC. The timed trial began at 22:55:54.161 UTC (6:55:54 p.m. Eastern), with a fixed cutoff at 23:10:54.161 UTC. All workers stopped, and the last publisher had exited, by 23:10:32.863 UTC. Setup took 23.07 minutes; active trial time was 14.65 minutes. Administrative reporting and preservation after this point receive no throughput credit.

The sample contained 120 Firefox and 12 Thunderbird origins, 800,990 source bytes and 1,008 frozen obligations. It reused existing structural maps and excluded 498 previously analyzed/read origins plus 3,031 Suite origins. Six binary/non-UTF8 failures and ten parser failures stayed in the sample. These known limits already capped this tool version at 116 possible accepted origins, so this diagnostic run could not pass 132/132. Negative-syntax tests and templates are tool limitations, not proof their source cannot be understood.

## What was built

The tool stores specific unit explanations and applicable facts, shared contracts, exact source anchors, independent review receipts, and a fixed submission deadline. A later file can reference a previously accepted contract while retaining its own context checks. It preserves prior records and separates generated facts from behavioral judgment.

Code: [tb-tools trial branch](https://github.com/arschmitz/tb-tools/tree/ingestion-compact-trial-20261013). Initial revision `37478cbd3ee8766fb5523c44c7eba4f8fb39fcbd`; repaired revision `68ebea8b5c85d3dab6d483b023bd34e23bd509dc`. Clean checks passed 30 tests initially and 31 after the repair. A separate dirty-checkout review ran 32 tests because it includes one pre-existing grouped-adapter test.

## Failures that determined the result

1. At 22:59:04 UTC, Git rejected an extra final blank line in an exported note. A command-scoped whitespace setting preserved immutable bytes and left other checks enabled.
2. At 23:02:03 UTC, the knowledge reader rejected shared-contract notes missing `source.reference`. The repair added checked source links and new record identities. Prior drafts were retained. The repair time stayed inside the trial.
3. At 23:09:48 UTC, local exact retrieval passed **86/86** notes, but standalone retrieval returned the required IDs for only **84/86**. Two distinct records had the same shared-contract title. The publisher stopped before committing or pushing evidence. The exact cause of that retrieval difference remains unresolved.
The shared-contract drafts also have empty `paths` metadata despite their source links. That scope-format limitation remains unresolved. These drafts were not promoted to shared knowledge.


The queue contains 19 accepted behavior records and 67 supporting notes in the final 86-note contribution. They remain drafts. One accepted `resource2` fixture record omitted two direct backend test callers. An independently checked additive correction is preserved. It does not retroactively earn timing credit.

## What reuse demonstrated

Accepted cross-file contract references: **1**. Reviewed strict body-rule or exact-body reuse members: **0**. The reused contract describes a test harness. This did not demonstrate large-scale reuse of function-body behavior. The design reduced record repetition, but the run did not show a material source-analysis speed increase.

## Coverage and limits

The accepted records cover scoped tests, fixtures, references, an imported architecture alias declaration, and their checked consumers. Examples include module/microtask error completion, iframe navigation protection, CSS overflow references, String.raw NaN handling, and build resource validation. They do not establish whole-engine understanding. No product tests ran, and no new Thunderbird–Firefox behavior chain was validated in this sample.

The task retained the per-origin JSON report, drafts, and raw receipts as private audit artifacts. They are not published by this summary note. The measured counts and limits are recorded here for shared retrieval. Local retrieval used the actual local store through bounded exact-section search. Standalone retrieval used the clean published reader and a contribution-only cache. Full console UI, full-library search, semantic ranking, and broader behavior-query quality were not tested.

Source pins: Thunderbird `87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799`; Firefox `1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b`.

This result does not support rolling this process out over the full repositories or claiming completion in under 1,000 hours. A successful publication repair alone would still leave the measured review rate far below the target.
